title: Cap. X: Bellarmine — in/cum Adamo peccasse; figurative speech / deny if = imputation
pass_a_gloss: Unless we posit, says Bellarmine, that we truly sinned in Adam and with Adam, there will be no way to explain how there is any true guilt in newly born infants, and this Catholic dogma will seem not so much above reason as against reason. Before going on: what is it to sin in and with Adam? The phrase must be figurative. Perhaps it means Adam's sin is imputed to us. That being posited, Placeus denies that proposition.
pass_b_english: Unless we grant, he says, that we truly sinned in Adam and with Adam, there is no way to explain how newborn infants bear any true guilt, and this Catholic dogma will look not merely above reason but against it. Before we go further: what does it mean to sin in and with Adam? The phrase has to be figurative. Perhaps it means Adam's sin is imputed to us. Take that reading, and I deny the proposition.
source_text: Nisi ponamus, inquit, nos in Adamo, & cum Adamo vere peccasse, nulla ratione explicari poterit, quomodo in parvulis recens natis sit aliqua vera culpa, & hoc Catholicum dogma, non tam supra rationem, quam contra rationem esse videbitur. Antequam progrediamur, quid est in & cum Adamo peccare? Figuratam enim profecto locutionem esse oportet. Fortasse est nobis Adami peccatum imputari. Hoc posito, propositionem illam nego.

choices.decision: figurative; if = imputation of Adam's sin, Placeus denies the proposition

notes: Cap. X Theologorum auxilium densify section 119 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 124–127 tip).
